SCOPE: our 5 CURRENTLY fully-supported games. For EACH, tell me what product options, versions, modloaders, plugins/mods, and config knobs we should be offering that we may be missing. Games: (1) Minecraft, (2) Rust, (3) Valheim, (4) Counter-Strike 2 (CS2), (5) Palworld.

For EACH game return a structured section with:
- **Editions/versions to offer as a picker**: e.g. Minecraft Java vs Bedrock; modloaders Vanilla/Paper/Spigot/Purpur/Fabric/Forge/NeoForge/Quilt + version selection & snapshots; Rust vanilla vs staging/modded (Oxide/uMod vs Carbon); Valheim vanilla vs BepInEx-modded (Valheim Plus / ValheimPlus successor); CS2 game modes (competitive/casual/deathmatch/retake/surf/practice) + Metamod/CounterStrikeSharp/SourceMod plugins + Steam Workshop maps; Palworld config/mods.
- **Top mods/plugins ecosystem** an owner would expect us to one-click (name the actual mod managers, plugin platforms, popular mods/plugins).
- **Key editable config file(s)** and the specific settings owners tune (we already map server.properties, PalWorldSettings.ini). List the file + the 8-15 most-tuned keys per game.
- **SteamCMD app ID** (server) where applicable, and the server start/update mechanism.
- **Resource baseline** (RAM/CPU guidance per player-count tier).
- **"What we're missing" verdict**: the 3-5 highest-value options/features to add for this game.

Be concrete and buildable — this feeds real backend config + a deploy-wizard options UI. Include source URLs. Return a thorough itemized report.

Also popular Fabric/Forge performance mods (Lithium, Ferium, etc.) and modpack one-click installs.

I've found comprehensive information about Palworld dedicated server configuration including REST API and RCON setup. Here's what I found:

## OptionSettings Configuration

Palworld stores many settings inside the long OptionSettings=(...) line in the PalWorldSettings.ini file. Every setting lives in PalWorldSettings.ini, under the [/Script/Pal.PalGameWorldSettings] line as part of the long OptionSettings=(...) string.

## REST API Setup

To enable the Palworld REST API, set RESTAPIEnabled=True and a RESTAPIPort in PalWorldSettings.ini. REST API is Palworld's newer, HTTP-based interface that returns clean JSON and is ideal if you're writing your own automation, dashboards or scripts with curl, Python or Node.

These endpoints can return information such as the server version, server name, world identifier, server FPS, current player count, frame time, uptime, base count, and number of in-game days.

## RCON Setup

To turn on RCON, set AdminPassword="your-strong-password", RCONEnabled=True, and RCONPort=25575 (or any free port) in OptionSettings.

However, Palworld's older RCON system has been deprecated, and Pocketpair recommends moving to the REST API because RCON is scheduled to stop functioning in a future update.

## Important Notes

- Always stop the server before editing the .ini, as Palworld rewrites this file on shutdown, so any change made while it's running gets overwritten on the next restart.
- Set a strong AdminPassword before enabling RCON or the REST API — both need it, and anyone with it can wipe the server.
- You can enable both RCON and REST API at once — they don't conflict.

## DeathPenalty Options

DeathPenalty has four options: None, Item, ItemAndEquipment, and All. Here's what each does:

- **None** - keep everything
- **Item** - drop inventory contents; keep equipment (weapons, armor, accessories, gliders)
- **ItemAndEquipment** - drop both items and equipment
- **All** - enables permadeath with full loss of items and Pals

## Hardcore Mode

For hardcore mode, set bHardcore=True and bPalLost=True with increased enemy and Pal damage.

## CrossplayPlatforms

The CrossplayPlatforms setting in PalWorldSettings.ini controls which platforms can connect; the default is (Steam,Xbox,PS5,Mac). For example, set CrossplayPlatforms=(Steam) to allow only Steam players.

## bAllowGlobalPalboxExport

bAllowGlobalPalboxExport allows sending Pals to global inter-server storage, with a default of True; when set to False, players cannot export Pals off the server. Export is on by default, while import is disabled on dedicated servers by default.

All gameplay settings, including DeathPenalty, sit inside a single OptionSettings=(...) line in the configuration file, comma-separated.
